items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: it would pay Ormond $25 or $30 a week... I said, I'd love to do it... I was able to start playing at such an early age, especially in a place like a dance hall.

ctx.x: You say there were no other of the second generation jazz musicians in this young group that you led with? Not at that time.

Not at that time. I had not yet come in contact with anyone. This came later, after I played at this little theater down here. There was a drummer, who I must confess that my memory is just failing me a little bit at this point here, who was working at the Furn Dance Hall. And he met my father and told my father, he said, there is a very good position open at a dance hall. He says, and it would pay Ormond $25 or $30 a week. Well, I was only 14 years old at the time. And when he told me that, I said, gee, I said,…

get off, my uncle would pass around the fern and he would see that I got on a streetcar and got home. So this was the only way that I was able to start playing at such an early age, especially in a place like a dance hall.
